[0] HTTP caching - revision notes
[1] A cache stores a copy of a response so that later requests for the same resource can be answered without contacting the origin server.
[2] The Cache-Control response header tells caches how to behave.
[3] The max-age directive sets how many seconds a response stays fresh.
[4] A fresh response can be reused without asking the server.
[5] Once it is stale, the cache must revalidate it before reuse.
[6] Revalidation uses validators.
[7] The ETag header carries an identifier for a specific version of a resource.
[8] The client sends it back in an If-None-Match header.
[9] If the resource has not changed, the server replies with status 304 Not Modified and no body, which saves bandwidth.
[10] The no-store directive means a response must not be kept in any cache.
[11] It is used for sensitive data such as account pages.
[12] The no-cache directive does not mean "do not cache".
[13] It means the cache may store the response but must revalidate it with the server before every reuse.
[14] Shared caches such as CDNs sit between many users and the origin.
[15] The private directive limits a response to the user's own browser cache.
[16] A common pattern for static assets is to put a content hash in the file name and send a very long max-age, so a changed file gets a new URL and old copies never need invalidating.
</source>

items.quote: A cache stores a copy of a response so that later requests for the same resource can be answered without contacting the origin server.
items.idea: Caching saves time and resources by storing copies of responses so subsequent requests don't need to hit the original server.

items.quote: The Cache-Control response header tells caches how to behave.
items.idea: The Cache-Control header dictates the rules for how caches should handle a response.

items.quote: The max-age directive sets how many seconds a response stays fresh.
items.idea: The max-age directive specifies the duration, in seconds, that a response is considered valid.

items.quote: Once it is stale, the cache must revalidate it before reuse.
items.idea: After a response becomes stale, the cache is required to check with the server before using it again.

items.quote: The ETag header carries an identifier for a specific version of a resource.
items.idea: ETags provide a unique identifier for a particular version of a resource.

items.quote: The no-store directive means a response must not be kept in any cache.
items.idea: The no-store directive ensures that a response cannot be saved in any cache.
